claim: NASA highlighted a satellite-gravimetry study identifying 40 regions where terrestrial water-storage trends were significantly associated with human activities.
verifiedFacts: NASA Earth Observatory published October 20 analysis of GRACE and GRACE-FO measurements from April 2002 to November 2025.
Researchers identified 40 regions with strong associations between water-storage trends and activities including irrigation, reservoirs and land-use change.
NASA reports five- to tenfold greater spatial detail than earlier analyses at the cost of temporal resolution.
inference: Inference: provenance-rich civic and ecological visualizations could expose uncertainty, spatial resolution and competing causal explanations instead of selling unqualified regenerative outcomes.
Actors: NASA researchers/data providers; water planners and land stewards are prospective users, not verified buyers.
Consultancy: Water Stewardship Evidence Map as a demonstration; client problem is interpreting regional changes without conflating association with causation.
Disposition: qt314wink/seed-loom CORE; MelodicBloom/project-constellation INCUBATE for visualization; Kozo Dreams REFERENCE-ONLY for ecological context; extends regenerative intelligence thesis.
significance: A new high-resolution observational layer supports bounded civic/regenerative data visualization and measurement literacy.
assumptions: Open data can be appropriately downscaled to relevant client geography.
knownLimitations: Associations are not direct causal proof.
Resolution gain sacrifices temporal detail; no client procurement evidence.
